decisions.statement: A declaration is generated where its page states the command writing that declaration again.
Every other declaration is written by hand.
Which declarations are generated is read from their pages rather than from a path.
A method is a member of an interface a generated declaration has.
A member typed as a function is a method as a method signature is.
A global is a declared function or a declared name whose type is callable.
A hand-written global naming a method and no generated global is refused.
A name the generated declarations also carry as a global is let through.
The refusal names the line the declaration sits on.
Every declaration the index has is judged rather than the ones a change has.
A declaration a compiler believes fails at nothing until the game runs.
A generated declaration file that is not there refuses the run.
A hand-written declaration file that is not there is judged as nothing.
No file is let off by name.

definition: the check refusing a hand-written global the generated declarations carry only as a method
